html:
Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, began as Pishpek, a clay fort built in 1825 by the Khanate of Kokand to control the Chuy valley and its Kyrgyz herders.

Russian troops took and destroyed the fort in 1862. A Russian market town grew up on the site, settled by Slav farmers and by Dungans from China. In 1926 the Soviets renamed it Frunze, after the Red Army commander Mikhail Frunze, born there, and made it the capital of the Kyrgyz republic.

Planned on a Soviet grid with wide tree-lined streets, it became a factory town during the Second World War when plants were moved east. It took back the Kyrgyz form of its old name in 1991. The protests that overthrew presidents in the Tulip Revolution of 2005 and 2010 were fought out in its central square.
sum: Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, began as Pishpek, a clay fort built in 1825 by the Khanate of Kokand to control the Chuy valley and its Kyrgyz herders.
